detail.longDescription: I was trying to write a code that speaks a paragraph when a user types in a certain input, using pyttsx3 as my only approach. The below is a simplification of my program: from pyttsx3 import init req = input(>>>).strip() raEngine = init() try: while True: match req.upper(): case 'STALIN': para = 'Joseph Stalin...' print(para) ... case _: print(f'{req} is not a valid paragraph name.') para = '' raEngine.say(para) raEngine.runAndWait() except (KeyboardInterrupt,EOFError): print('Cheerio!') However, running this code, I get the error: Traceback (most recent call last): File "/home/ubuntu/.local/lib/python3.13/site-packages/pyttsx3/__init__.py", line 22, in init eng = _activeEngines[driverName] ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/usr/local/lib/python3.13/weakref.py", line 136, in __getitem__ o = self.data[key]() ~~~~~~~~~^^^^^ KeyError: None During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred: Traceback (most recent call last): File "project.py",line 3, in <module> raEngine = init() File "/home/ubuntu/.local/lib/python3.13/site-packages/pyttsx3/__init__.py", line 24, in init eng = Engine(driverName, debug) File "/home/ubuntu/.local/lib/python3.13/site-packages/pyttsx3/engine.py", line 59, in __init__ self.proxy = driver.DriverProxy(weakref.proxy(self), self.driver_name, debug) ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/home/ubuntu/.local/lib/python3.13/site-packages/pyttsx3/driver.py", line 43, in __init__ self._driver = self._module.buildDriver(weakref.proxy(self)) ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/home/ubuntu/.local/lib/python3.13/site-packages/pyttsx3/drivers/espeak.py", line 20, in buildDriver return EspeakDriver(proxy) File "/home/ubuntu/.local/lib/python3.13/site-packages/pyttsx3/drivers/espeak.py", line 54, in __init__ self.setProperty("voice", EspeakDriver._defaultVoice) ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/home/ubuntu/.local/lib/python3.13/site-packages/pyttsx3/drivers/espeak.py", line 135, in setProperty raise ValueError(msg) ValueError: SetVoiceByName failed with unknown return code -1 for voice: gmw/en So from there I could conclude that it seems to be that the initiation of pyttsx3 has an issue. When I looked into the code of espeak.py (where eSpeak is accompanying pyttsx3), I found out about the staticmethod for the EspeakDriver class, called setProperty which is the method from which the ValueError is being raised. This method takes in two parameters: name and value as per the below: @staticmethod def setProperty(name: str, value): # noqa: C901,PLR0912 if name == "voice": if value is None: return try: utf8Value = str(value).encode("utf-8") logging.debug(f"Attempting to set voice to: {value}") # noqa: G004 result = _espeak.SetVoiceByName(utf8Value) if result == 0: # EE_OK is 0 logging.debug(f"Successfully set voice to: {value}") # noqa: G004 elif result == 1: # EE_BUFFER_FULL msg = f"SetVoiceByName failed: EE_BUFFER_FULL while setting voice to {value}" raise ValueError(msg) elif result == 2: # EE_INTERNAL_ERROR msg = f"SetVoiceByName failed: EE_INTERNAL_ERROR while setting voice to {value}" raise ValueError(msg) else: msg = ( "SetVoiceByName failed with unknown return code " f"{result} for voice: {value}" ) raise ValueError(msg) except ctypes.ArgumentError as e: msg = f"Invalid voice name: {value}, error: {e}" raise ValueError(msg) Further looking into this code, I could figure out that value is indeed the voice gmw/en from which the return code -1 originates. Furthermore, I could also conclude that the return code -1 further originates from _espeak.SetVoiceByName(utf8Value) wherein utf8value is an encoded version of the string gmw/en However, I cannot really find the code from which _espeak originates, since it is written as: from . import _espeak The system from which this error arises is Linux Ubuntu. I have also run the following terminal line: sudo apt update && sudo apt install espeak ffmpeg libespeak1 and yet the error still arises. Is there any way of overriding this?
